claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let me start with: **Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child - my son Alex. He's 8 years old and I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one child, Alex, who is 8 years old.

To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask you a few questions:

**Does Alex live with you in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives with me here in the UK. We're in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Alex lives with you in Manchester.

**Are you currently living in the UK, and do you have the right to reside here?** (For example, are you a UK citizen, or do you have settled status, or another immigration status that allows you to live in the UK?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK and I have the right to be here.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for confirming that.

Now, just to make sure there are no special circumstances that might affect your eligibility:

**Is Alex currently in hospital, in care, or living in any residential accommodation, or has anyone else claimed Child Benefit for him?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, he was actually in care for a short while earlier this year, but he's back home with me now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I see, thank you for letting me know. That's an important detail.

**Can you tell me how long Alex was in care, and does he now spend at least 24 hours a week at home with you? Also, is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for him?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He was in care for about 7 weeks, but he's been back home with me full-time since then. No one else is claiming Child Benefit for him - it's just me looking after him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. That's very helpful.

Just one final question to complete my assessment:

**Are you or your partner (if you have one) earning over £60,000 per year?** 

(This won't affect whether you can *get* Child Benefit, but it may mean you need to pay a tax charge on it, so it's good to be aware of.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'd rather not go into my income details right now - I'm mainly just trying to find out if I'm actually eligible to claim it in the first place.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's absolutely fine - I have enough information to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me provide you with my assessment:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news! You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:
- Alex is 8 years old (under 16)
- He lives with you full-time in the UK
- You have the right to reside in the UK
- Although Alex was in care for 7 weeks earlier this year, this is under the 8-week threshold that would affect eligibility
- Since Alex is now back home with you full-time and no one else is claiming Child Benefit for him, you meet all the criteria

You can proceed with making a claim for Child Benefit. If you haven't already claimed, you'll need to make a new claim for Alex.

reasonings: Alex is 8 years old (under 16), lives with you full-time in the UK, and you have the right to reside in the UK. Although Alex was in care for 7 weeks earlier this year, this is under the 8-week threshold after which Child Benefit payments would normally stop. Since Alex is now back home with you full-time and no one else is claiming Child Benefit for him, you meet all the eligibility criteria. You are responsible for Alex as he lives with you, and there are no special circumstances preventing you from claiming.
